text:
Alex: quick q — what's our recommended pattern for mapping API errors to exceptions in the SDKs? should we always surface request_id in the exception?
Priya: yes, include request_id. makes debugging so much easier when customers paste stack traces. use header X-Request-ID or our response.request_id field. :+1:
Sam: agreed. i'd add a small error class hierarchy: ApiError(base), ClientError(4xx), ServerError(5xx), RateLimitError(429) with retry_after if present.
Marta: for streaming endpoints it's trickier — partial_response vs connection_reset. do we throw on first stream error or attach an error to the stream object?
Devin: for streaming i'd expose a StreamError events + raise if the stream cannot recover. don't lose the tokens already yielded. consumers can decide to continue or abort.
Alex: good point. so exception vs event depends on sync vs async iterator semantics?
Priya: exactly. in Python async iterator, raise on iteration if unrecoverable. for chunk-level transient errors, emit a warning and attach request_id.
Sam: a couple of language specifics we decided last sprint:
- Python: ApiError with attrs (status_code, error_code, message, request_id, raw_body)
- JS: extend Error, put .code, .requestId, .status
- Go: error types implementing interface with Status() and RequestID()
Marta: can we standardize the header name? some SDKs look at `x-request-id`, some `x-redwood-request-id`.
Alex: let's standardize on `X-Request-ID` for incoming client requests and `X-Redwood-Request-ID` for the backend generated id. SDK should prefer the response header `X-Redwood-Request-ID` if present.
Priya: also map retry info: if 429 or 503 and there's Retry-After header, attach retry_after to the exception and expose a .should_retry property.
Devin: pseudo for Python raising:
```
class ApiError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status, code, msg, request_id=None, retry_after=None, raw=None):
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = msg
        self.request_id = request_id
        self.retry_after = retry_after
        self.raw = raw
        super().__init__(f"{status} {code}: {msg} (rid={request_id})")
```
Sam: and log debug lines like `logger.debug("api-response", extra={"rid": request_id, "status": status, "path": path})` — keep structured logging.
Marta: FYI for Node streams: the fetch stream may emit 'error' after partial data; we should emit a StreamPartialError that includes bytes_received and request_id.
Maria: quick question: do we want SDK automatically to retry for idempotent operations? what's the list? GET, embeddings, and a few generation endpoints when you pass deterministic flags?
Priya: automatic retries only for idempotent ops (embeddings, embeddings-batch, rerank) and for status codes 502/503/504/429 with backoff. For generator endpoints we provide an opt-in retry flag, default off.
Alex: can someone add a short snippet to the SDK guidelines doc and a test that asserts request_id is attached to exceptions + logs?
Devin: i'll open a PR. pinging @Maria for Python impl review once done.
Maria: happy to review. can you also add a lint rule to ensure exceptions include request_id in their __str__? small but helps.
dev-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/472 — title: "sdk: attach request_id + retry info to ApiError"
Alex: nice, thanks. reviewers: @Maria @Priya @Sam — quick review would be great, aim to merge before EOD tomorrow.
Priya: also add a unit test for streaming partial error shape.
Sam: +1, i'll add a Go test for error type assertions.
Marta: thanks all — this should reduce customer debug cycles a lot. :pray:
